status: candidate verdicts for operator review; not a gate. overturned=true means the advocate lifts the reader's borderline to yes; overturned=false means the reader's doubt stands and the final is no.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds. Both classify clinically diagnosed MCI against cognitively normal older adults from T1 structural MRI (P-52: 3D T1WI hippocampal radiomics, one Chinese hospital; P-99: FreeSurfer morphometry 'from T1w MRI data', Moscow memory clinic plus health-examination volunteers). The reader's doubt is P-52's Table 1: NC MoCA 22.53 +/- 2.91 and MMSE 25.73 +/- 2.55 against a stated NC criterion of MoCA >= 27. That is an internal inconsistency in how P-52 reports its control label, not a different population class of the kind condition 1 excludes (for example Parkinson's patients against Alzheimer's-spectrum MCI). The batch treated the same kind of defect in P-50 (stated MCI MMSE 25-26 against a Table 1 MCI MMSE of 28.0) as a label-definition candidate explanation in C-01, which the skeptic confirmed as yes. Applied identically, condition 1 holds here, with the inconsistency carried as a candidate explanation. If the NC group really were impaired on screening, label noise would lower P-52's AUC, so it cannot account for P-52 being the higher of the two.
conditions_attacked.2_metric: Holds on AUC with AUC. The record set P-52's AUC against P-99's accuracy; P-52 prints no test accuracy, so the pair is judged on AUC.
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Holds. P-99 reports no hippocampal-only or radiomic classifier and no held-out split; P-52 reports no whole-brain morphometry model and nothing on another cohort. P-99's own XGBoost (ROC-AUC 0.644 +/- 0.149) differs from P-52 only in features and cohort, which are allowed differences, and it widens the gap rather than closing it.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Holds as worded, and robustly in the qualifying direction. P-99 prints no interval (0.735 +/- 0.076 is a fold spread). Hanley-McNeil with 145 MCI/62 HC: Q1 = 0.735/1.265 = 0.581, Q2 = 2(0.735^2)/1.735 = 0.623, SE = sqrt([0.735*0.265 + 144*(0.581-0.540) + 61*(0.623-0.540)]/(145*62)) = 0.0351, interval 0.666-0.804. P-52's 0.864 lies 0.060 above it. It also lies above the fold-based alternatives: 0.735 +/- 1.96*0.076/sqrt(10) = 0.688-0.782, and with t(9) = 2.262, 0.681-0.789. The reverse fails only by 0.005, against P-52's printed lower bound (0.73), and does not matter under the one-directional wording ('One study's estimate must lie outside the other's 95% interval'). That wording is the reading on which C-80, C-82, C-83, C-121 and C-204 qualified after skeptic review. Two-sample z: 2.02 (Hanley-McNeil for both; P-52 SE 0.0535), 2.20 (P-52 Hanley-McNeil against P-99's fold SE 0.024), 1.68 (P-52's printed lower half-width 0.134/1.96 = 0.068). P-52's asymmetric printed interval enters only the non-qualifying direction.
conditions_attacked.5_performance_validity: Holds. P-52 test AUC 0.864 (training 0.935); P-99 0.735. Neither is at or above 0.97.
conditions_attacked.6_record: The record compares P-52's AUC with P-99's accuracy. On the printed AUCs, the gap survives.

figures.P-52: Test AUC 0.864, printed 95% CI 0.73-0.89 (asymmetric), test set 30 MCI/15 NC from a 7:3 split of 150. For reference, Hanley-McNeil 30/15: SE 0.0535, 0.759-0.969. Training AUC 0.935 (0.83-0.97).
figures.P-99: 10-fold CV on 207 (145 MCI/62 HC), RBF SVC ROC-AUC 0.735 +/- 0.076 (fold SD). Derived Hanley-McNeil 0.666-0.804; fold-based 0.688-0.782 (z) or 0.681-0.789 (t9). P-52's 0.864 lies outside every construction.

candidate_explanations: Control label (P-52): the stated criterion and Table 1 disagree. P-52 p.2: 'Forty-five participants with normal MoCA performance (MoCA score >=27) ... served as the normal control (NC) group'; Table 1 p.3: 'MoCA score 21.65 +/- 3.86 22.53 +/- 2.91 0.17'.
MCI label (P-99): an ICD-10 F06.7 memory-clinic diagnosis in patients over 65. P-99 p.3: 'Patients over the age of 65 who had been diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (F06.7) were eligible.'

Features within the MRI channel: seven hippocampal radiomic texture/wavelet features from deep-learning segmentation (P-52) against up to 500 of 906 whole-brain FreeSurfer features selected by chi-squared SelectKBest (P-99). P-52 p.1: 'A total of 1183 radiomic features were systematically extracted from the bilateral hippocampus of each subject.'

Preprocessing scope (P-52): features were z-scored against the whole cohort, and the hypothesis-test filter is not stated to be confined to the training set; Section 3.5 names feature selection on the full sample as a candidate mechanism. P-52 p.2: 'µ corresponds to the mean feature value across the entire patient cohort'; p.3: 'Subsequent hypothesis testing identified 252 radiomic features ... showing statistically significant intergroup differences.'

Validation design and size: one random 45-subject test split (P-52) against 10-fold CV on 207 with a grid search inside the same CV (P-99). P-52 p.2: 'an independent test set that contained 30 MCI patients and 15 NC subjects'.
Classifier: XGBoost (P-52) against RBF SVC (P-99); P-99's own XGBoost gave 0.644 +/- 0.149 on its data. P-99 p.4: 'the best and most stable results were obtained by SVC (0.68 F1, 0.735 ROC -AUC)'.
Age imbalance in P-99 (MCI 73.9 +/- 7.3 vs HC 68.9 +/- 5.3 years), which would favour P-99's discrimination and so runs against the observed gap.
Scanner: 1.5 T Toshiba (P-99); P-52's acquisition protocol is in its supplement, not in the extract.
None of these is shown by either paper to be sufficient.
results.reason: Every condition holds on the sources. P-52's 0.864 lies outside P-99's derived interval under every construction (Hanley-McNeil 0.666-0.804; fold-based 0.681-0.789). The reverse failing by 0.005 does not matter under the one-directional wording on which C-80, C-82, C-83, C-121 and C-204 qualified, and two of three two-sample constructions give z of 2.0 or more. The reader's condition-1 doubt is P-52's contradictory control statistics. That is the same kind of defect C-01 carried as a label-definition candidate explanation, not a different population class, so the same treatment applies here. The report should say that the gap rests on P-52's single 45-subject split and that P-52's control label is internally inconsistent.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds. 3-year (36-month) pMCI vs sMCI in ADNI from baseline MRI. P-72's reported model fuses sMRI with FDG-PET (MRI channel shared), and P-72 also prints an sMRI-only arm.
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Fails on the recorded metric. P-72's sMRI-only MAResNet18 arm is P-3's input condition (T1 MRI alone, same horizon). Its accuracy of 73.68% against P-3's 74.61% agrees at every evaluation size: Wilson for P-72 is 61.0-83.4% at n=57 and 66.6-79.7% even pooled over three test sets (n=171); for P-3 it is 70.96-77.95% at n=593; z = 0.15. The papers' own data dissolve the accuracy gap that the record (on a misread 94.61%) claims.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Fails on P-72's reported model and is fragile on the ablation AUC. P-72's reported conversion result (77.19%, AUC 0.755) agrees with P-3 on both metrics at every n. Accuracy: P-72 64.8-86.2% (n=57) or 70.4-82.8% (n=171) contains 74.61%, and P-3's interval contains 77.19%. AUC: P-72 0.620-0.890 (22/35) or 0.678-0.833 (66/105) contains 0.780, and P-3's 0.743-0.817 contains 0.755. The only crossing is the sMRI-arm AUC: 0.721 lies 0.022 below P-3's Hanley-McNeil lower bound (0.743), in one direction only (z = 0.79 at n=57, 1.30 pooled). It disappears under P-3's own printed fold variance (0.003, so SD 0.055; t(4) interval 0.780 +/- 2.776*0.055/sqrt(5) = 0.712-0.848). It also sits inside the interval of P-3's own plain 3D CNN on the same splits (AUC 0.758, Hanley-McNeil 0.719-0.797).
conditions_attacked.5_performance_validity: Holds: no conversion figure is near 0.97.
conditions_attacked.6_record: The recorded 94.61% is P-72's AD vs NC accuracy. On the printed conversion figures, the claimed gap does not exist.

figures.P-72: sMCI vs pMCI, 238/151, subject-level 70/15/15 split averaged over three different test sets (about 57 each: 22 pMCI/35 sMCI). sMRI-only 73.68%: Wilson 61.0-83.4% (n=57), 66.6-79.7% (n=171). sMRI-only AUC 0.721: Hanley-McNeil 0.580-0.862 (22/35), 0.640-0.802 (66/105). Multimodal 77.19%: 64.8-86.2% / 70.4-82.8%. Multimodal AUC 0.755: 0.620-0.890 / 0.678-0.833.
figures.P-3: 298 sMCI/295 pMCI, 5-fold CV: 74.61%, Wilson 70.96-77.95%. AUC 0.780: Hanley-McNeil SE 0.019, 0.743-0.817; from the fold variance 0.003, 0.732-0.828 (z) or 0.712-0.848 (t4).

candidate_explanations: Architecture: P-3's CAAT ensemble against P-72's MAResNet18. P-3's own baseline 3D CNN on the same splits gives 70.84% and AUC 0.758, so architecture moves AUC by 0.022 within P-3. P-3 p.7: 'Baseline 3D CNN 0.71 (0.005) 0.71 (0.003) 0.71 (0.003) 70.84 (0.001) 0.758 (0.003)'.
Input representation: whole 3D T1 image (P-3) against a grey-matter map (P-72).

Cohort: the Wen et al. ADNI1/2 benchmark (298/295) against subjects with paired baseline MRI and FDG-PET (238/151). P-3 p.6: 'The dataset consists of 298 sMCI and 295 pMCI participants retrieved from datasets ANDI1 and ADNI2.'

Validation: 5-fold CV over 593 against three hold-out test sets of about 57. P-72 p.6: 'We followed the same data split strategy to construct three different subsets with different test sets, the average of three classification accuracies is used as the final result.'

sMCI label: P-3 requires the diagnosis to remain MCI through 36 months; P-72 states no follow-up minimum for sMCI. P-3 p.3: 'if the patient's diagnosis remained as MCI, we categorized him/her as sMCI.'
results.reason: The strongest case for qualifying is the literal per-metric reading: the sMRI-only arm's AUC (0.721) lies outside P-3's Hanley-McNeil interval, the same one-directional test that qualified C-80. It does not carry. On the matched figure, the accuracies are essentially equal (73.68% vs 74.61%, z = 0.15), so the papers' own data dissolve the recorded gap (condition 3). P-72's reported model agrees with P-3 on both metrics at every evaluation size (condition 4). The AUC crossing is 0.022 in one direction, not significant (z 0.79-1.30), and gone under P-3's printed fold variance. In C-80, by contrast, both metrics crossed and the crossing survived P-3's fold-based interval. Final no, on conditions 3 and 4.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds. Both predict conversion within three years (pMCI vs sMCI) in ADNI MCI from baseline T1 MRI. P-82 p.2: 'converted to AD at longitudinal visits within three years'; P-72 p.3: 'MCI subjects who developed AD within 3 years were labeled as pMCI'. P-72's reported model adds FDG-PET; its sMRI-only arm uses MRI alone, as P-82 does.
conditions_attacked.2_metric: Holds: AUC with AUC and accuracy with accuracy.
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Holds: the matched figure widens the gap rather than reconciling it. The figure under P-82's condition (MRI alone, same horizon) is P-72's sMRI-only MAResNet18 arm (73.68%, AUC 0.721). AUC: each lies outside the other's interval at every P-72 evaluation size (0.888 against 0.580-0.862 at 22/35 and 0.640-0.802 at 66/105; 0.721 against P-82's 0.745-1.0). Accuracy: the reader's agreement is not 0.1 point but 0.02 point (20/24 = 83.33% against an upper bound of 83.35%). It exists only if P-72's averaged figure is treated as one 57-subject test. P-72 states that the figure is the mean over 'three different subsets with different test sets', so it rests on more than 57 test evaluations. At n=58 the Wilson upper bound is 83.29%, at n=66 82.8%, and pooled (n=171) 66.6-79.7%, all excluding 83.33%. The matched accuracies therefore differ in one direction and the matched AUCs in both, so the matched figure does not dissolve the pair. On P-72's multimodal figure, the one that adds PET, the agreement at n=57 is also at the edge: 0.888 lies inside 0.620-0.890 by 0.002 and 0.755 inside 0.745-1.0 by 0.010. At pooled n, both of P-82's figures lie outside P-72's multimodal intervals (accuracy 70.4-82.8%; AUC 0.678-0.833). Condition 3 directs the comparison to the figure under the other's condition, and that figure is the sMRI arm.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Holds. Matched AUC: excluded in both directions (two-sample z 1.63 at n=57, 1.99 pooled). Matched accuracy: excluded in one direction at any n above 57 (z 1.01 to 1.16). For consistency, C-80 (P-82 against P-3, confirmed yes by the skeptic) qualified on a one-directional AUC exclusion with z = 1.43 and a one-directional accuracy exclusion. The gap here is larger (0.167 vs 0.108 AUC) and excluded in both directions.
conditions_attacked.6_record: The recorded 94.61% is P-72's AD vs NC accuracy; the pair is judged on P-72's printed conversion figures, as in C-82.

figures.P-82: One random test set of 24 (11 pMCI/13 sMCI): 83.3% = 20/24, Wilson 64.1-93.3%; AUC 0.888, Hanley-McNeil (11/13) SE 0.073, 0.745-1.0 (capped). 10-fold CV only in Supplementary Table S2, not in the extract.

candidate_explanations: Input representation and architecture: FreeSurfer DKT tabular cortical features (volume, thickness, curvature, folding, area over 62 regions) with a transformer (P-82) against a 3D CNN on grey-matter maps (P-72). P-82 p.2: 'we extracted multiple cortical measurements including volume (VOL), cortical thickness (CT), curvature index (CD), folding index (FD), and surface area (SA) for 62 brain regions'.

Model selection on a small test set: P-82's 0.888 is the best of eight models scored on the same 24 subjects (AUC 0.542-0.888). P-82 p.4: 'GRU (AUC = 0.853) performs better than LSTM (AUC = 0.839) and RNN (AUC = 0.790)'.

sMCI label: P-82 counts MCI reverters to normal as sMCI; P-72 states no follow-up minimum. P-82 p.2: 'the subjects who were diagnosed as MCI at least twice, but reverse to a standard control, at last, are also considered as sMCI'.
Class balance: 145 pMCI/104 sMCI (58% pMCI) in P-82 against 151/238 (39% pMCI) in P-72; this bears on accuracy more than on AUC.
Cohort selection: P-72 is restricted to subjects with paired baseline MRI and FDG-PET. P-72 p.3: 'acquiring paired multimodal images from the same subject and from the closest acquisition date'.

Evaluation size and design: one random 24-subject test set (P-82) against three hold-out test sets of about 57, averaged (P-72). P-82 p.3: 'we split our 249 subjects randomly into three groups, including the training dataset (n = 200), the validation dataset (n = 25), and the testing dataset (n = 24).'
None of these is shown by either paper to be sufficient; P-82's 10-fold CV (Supplementary Table S2) could not be checked.
results.reason: Every condition holds on the matched figure. P-72's sMRI-only AUC (0.721) and P-82's 0.888 exclude each other at every evaluation size. The accuracy agreement the reader relied on is 0.02 point, and it exists only if P-72's mean over three different test sets is treated as a single 57-subject test; at any larger evaluation size 83.3% lies outside P-72's interval. This is a stronger case than C-80 (P-82 against P-3, confirmed yes on a one-directional exclusion), and consistency requires qualifying it. The report should carry P-82's single 24-subject test set, its best-of-eight model selection and the unavailable supplementary CV as fragilities.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds, on the printed binary figures: MCI vs healthy controls in ADNI from T1 structural MRI.
conditions_attacked.2_metric: Holds: accuracy with accuracy (AUC with AUC also available).
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Holds. P-109 has no subject-level split and no morphometric-feature model; P-125 has no slice model. P-109's other networks on the same slices (for example ConvNeXt 91.03% MCI/HC) share P-109's design, not P-125's.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Holds in both directions under every construction. P-125 prints a 95% margin of error ('The margin of error (MOE) was calculated with a confidence of 95 %'): 80.00 +/- 2.43% = 77.57-82.43%. Wilson gives 0.620-0.907 at n=28 (test size implied by its Table 6) and 0.627-0.905 at n=30. P-109's 94.23% lies outside all of these. P-109 prints no interval: Wilson at n=69 (10% of 685 subjects) is 0.861-0.977, at n=685 0.922-0.957, and on about 3,400 test slices 0.934-0.950. P-125's 80.00% lies outside all of these. AUC: 97.15 lies outside P-125's printed SVM 90.31 +/- 3.55 (86.76-93.86), and 0.9031 lies outside P-109's Hanley-McNeil interval (37/32: 0.932-1.0).
conditions_attacked.5_performance_validity: Holds on the rule as written. Section 3.5 states the exclusion conjunctively: 'internal-validation discrimination at or above 0.97 with small samples and no external cohort'. P-109 meets two limbs (MCI/HC AUC 0.9715 on internal validation; no external cohort). It fails the third: 'A total of 1075 individuals', 685 in this contrast, is larger than every Section 3.5 example. The same reading qualified C-46 (P-115 against P-109), which the skeptic confirmed as yes, and C-240 applied the letter in the same way. The review's own tagging reads P-109 at 0.9681, outside the suspect set. The compared accuracy (94.23%) is below 0.97 in any case. The slice-level shuffle is a mechanism Section 3.5 names as a candidate, not a limb of the rule, so it belongs among the candidate explanations. P-125 is not near ceiling.
conditions_attacked.6_record: The recorded 96.81% is P-109's three-class accuracy; the pair is judged on P-109's printed binary MCI/HC figure (94.23%, AUC 97.15%), which still exceeds P-125.

figures.P-125: 37 MCI/37 HC (ADNI, 1.5 T), 60/40 subject split; mean test accuracy 80.00 +/- 2.43% (printed 95% MOE, 77.57-82.43%; the spread is across five fold-models on one test partition); Wilson n=28: 0.620-0.907. Abstract 82.14%. Test AUC RF 85.71 +/- 2.8, SVM 90.31 +/- 3.55.
figures.P-109: BrainViT-L MCI/HC: accuracy 94.23%, AUC 97.15%; 370 MCI + 315 HC from 1075 subjects; about 50 slices per subject shuffled before a random 90/10 split. Wilson n=69: 0.861-0.977; n=685: 0.922-0.957. AUC Hanley-McNeil 37/32: 0.932-1.0.

candidate_explanations: Split unit: a random slice-level split, so slices of one subject can sit in both training and test sets (P-109), against a subject-level hold-out (P-125). Section 3.5 names this design as one that inflates reported accuracy. P-109 p.8: 'The images were shuffled randomly, and all experiments were carried out by splitting the data into 10 % for testing and 90 % for training.'

Input representation and unit of evaluation: about 50 2D slices per subject classified individually, against 8 amygdala morphometric scalars per subject. P-125 p.8: 'The features used for training were V, VN, DC, and TR for both hemispheres of the amygdala, for a total of 8 features.'

Sample size: 685 subjects in the contrast against 74, with a test partition of about 28-30 subjects in P-125. P-109 p.8: 'A total of 1075 individuals, including 390 with AD, 370 with MCI, and 315 HC, were used to create a balanced dataset for the 2D model.'
Architecture: a CNN-transformer hybrid on images against RF/SVM/KNN/ANN on hand-crafted features. P-109 p.10: '97.13 % with 98.52 % AUC for AD/HC and 94.23 % with 97.15 % for MCI/HC classifications'.
Participant selection: P-125's controls are restricted to MMSE 28-30 and CDR 0, and its MCI to MMSE 24-30 and CDR 0.5; P-109 does not state its selection criteria beyond ADNI diagnosis.
None of these is shown by either paper to be sufficient; the split unit is the leading candidate.
results.reason: Every condition holds on the sources. The binary MCI/HC figures (80.00% vs 94.23%) exclude each other in both directions under every interval construction, including P-125's own printed 95% margin. P-109 escapes the Section 3.5 exclusion on its small-sample limb, the reading that qualified C-46 against the same P-109 figures after skeptic review. The reader's open question is whether the exclusion extends to large cohorts evaluated on a slice-shuffled split. The rule as written does not extend it, and applying it identically requires qualifying this pair. The report should name the slice-level split as the leading candidate explanation and state that P-109 met the other two limbs of the exclusion.
